Kell High School|Carlton J. Kell]]
(Marietta, Georgia) | college = | career_start = 2021 | years1 = [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021]]–present | team1 = [[NBA G League Ignite]] | highlights = * [[NBA G League]] Next Up Game ([[2022–23 NBA G League season|2023]]) }} '''Sterling''' "'''Scoot'''" '''Henderson''' (born February 3, 2004) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[NBA G League Ignite]] of the [[NBA G League]]. He played for [[Carlton J. Kell High School]] in his hometown of [[Marietta, Georgia]], where he was a five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]]. At age 17, Henderson signed with the Ignite after graduating early from high school and became the youngest player in G League history. In his second season, he was selected as a [[captain (sports)|captain]] of the G League Next Up Game. Henderson is widely projected to be a top three pick in the [[2023 NBA draft]]. ==Early life== Henderson was born in [[Marietta, Georgia]] to Chris and Crystal Henderson.{{cite web |last=Abrams |first=Jonathan |title=Scoot Henderson Has Options. He's Choosing G League Ignite. |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/21/sports/basketball/scoot-henderson-g-league-ignite.html |website=[[The New York Times]] |access-date=May 21, 2021 |date=May 21, 2021}}{{cite web |title=Scoot Henderson Stats, Height, Weight, Position, Draft Status and more |url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/h/hendesc01.html |publisher=[[Sports Reference]] |access-date=19 January 2023}} His father is a coach and trainer, and his mother is a [[Health administration|healthcare administrator]]. His parents run the training facility Next Play 360° in Marietta, where they moved from [[Hempstead, New York]] shortly before Henderson's birth. He is the second youngest of seven siblings, including three sisters who played [[NCAA Division I]] basketball, and was nicknamed "Scoot" or "Scoota" because of how he would scoot across the floor as a baby.{{cite web |last=Beck |first=Howard |title=He Should Be in High School. Instead He's in the G League. And He's the Future. |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2021/11/18/scoot-henderson-g-league-ignite-daily-cover |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 19, 2023 |date=November 18, 2021}}{{cite web |last=Gordon |first=Sam |title=Hoop prodigy’s journey takes detour to Las Vegas |url=https://www.reviewjournal.com/sports/basketball/hoop-prodigys-journey-takes-detour-to-las-vegas-2650991/ |website=[[Las Vegas Review-Journal]] |access-date=January 20, 2023 |date=October 3, 2022}} ==High school career== Henderson played basketball for [[Carlton J. Kell High School]] in Marietta. During his freshman season, he came off the bench and played alongside his brother, C. J., a senior on the team.{{cite web |last=Conley |first=Tyhi |title=Battle-tested Kell team prepares for state tournament 21, 2023 |date=February 13, 2019}} In February 2020, during his sophomore season, Henderson scored a then career-high 49 points and made the game-winning shot in a 92–91 [[overtime (sports)|overtime]] win over [[Miller Grove High School (Georgia)|Miller Grove High School]] in the first round of the Class 5A state tournament.{{cite web |last=Carrington |first=Adam |date=February 20, 2020 |title=Scoota Henderson, Male AOW |url=https://www.mdjonline.com/scoota-henderson-male-aow/article_e67a2e24-542f-11ea-b96b-8b555e46e7cf.html |url-access=subscription |access-date=May 21, 2021 |access-date=January 20, 2023 |date=February 16, 2020}} He led Kell to the semifinals and averaged 24 points, six rebounds, three assists and three steals per game as a sophomore.{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |title=MaxPreps 2019-20 Boys Basketball Sophomore All-American Team |url=https://www.maxpreps.com/news/gdEsVKDwjkarlc6uLBrfnA/maxpreps-2019-20-boys-basketball-sophomore-all-american-team.htm |publisher=[[MaxPreps]] |access-date=January 20, 2023 |date=April 1, 2020}} Henderson was named Class 5A Player of the Year and first-team 5A All-State by ''[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]]''.{{cite web |last=Holcomb |first=Todd |title=2019-20 High school basketball All-State boys team |url=https://www.ajc.com/blog/high-school-sports/2019-high-school-basketball-all-state-boys-team/vTLurrXYusa3GlpDuB3uXL/ |website=[[The Atlanta Journal-Constitution]] |access-date=January 20, 2023 |date=March 26, 2020}} On January 22, 2021, as a junior, he scored 53 points in a 94–64 win against [[Osborne High School (Georgia)|Osborne High School]], breaking the |url=https://www.mdjonline.com/sports/henderson-sets-new-kell-scoring-marks/article_0119876e-6016-11eb-9eb5-9724a68a46d1.html |website=[[Marietta Daily Journal]] |access-date=January 21, 2023 |date=January 26, 2021}} Henderson led Kell to the Class 6A state title game, scoring 29 points in a loss to [[Wheeler High School (Georgia)|Wheeler High School]].{{cite web |last=Tec |first=Josh |title=Wheeler wins back-to-back state championships with victory over Kell |url=https://hoopseen.com/news/event/202103/wheeler-wins-back-back-state-championships-victory-over-kell |publisher=HoopSeen |access-date=January 21, 2023 |date=March 13, 2021}} He averaged 32 points, seven rebounds and six assists per game in the season,{{cite web |last=Divens |first=Jordan |title=2020-21 MaxPreps All-America Team: Chet Holmgren headlines high school basketball's best and most talented players senior high school season and head to NBA's G League Ignite |url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2021/05/21/fiver-star-recruit-bypass-senior-prep-season-nbas-minor-league/5207163001/ |website=[[USA Today]] |access-date=January 21, 2023 |date=May 21, 2021}} ===Recruiting=== Henderson was a consensus five-star [[college recruiting|recruit]], and [[247Sports.com|247Sports]] ranked him as the second-best [[point guard]] in the 2021 class.{{cite web |title=Scoot Henderson, 2021 Point Guard |url=https://n.rivals.com/content/athletes/scoot-henderson-259440?view=pv |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=January 21, 2023}}{{cite web |title=Scoot Henderson |url=http://www.espn.com/college-sports/basketball/recruiting/player/videos/_/id/242809 |publisher=[[247Sports.com|247Sports]] |access-date=January 21, 2023}} He drew the attention of [[NCAA Division I]] programs at camps following his freshman year of high school.{{cite web |last=McDonald |first=Dan |title=Four-star Scoot Henderson working his way through process |url=https://basketballrecruiting.rivals.com/news/four-star-scoot-henderson-working-his-way-through-process |publisher=[[Rivals.com|Rivals]] |access-date=January 20, 2023 |date=January 18, 2020}} He received his first Division I scholarship offer from [[Ole Miss Rebels men's basketball|Ole Miss]] and held offers from [[Florida Gators men's basketball|Florida]], [[Florida State Seminoles men's basketball|Florida State]] and [[Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets men's basketball|Georgia Tech]] by his sophomore season.{{cite web |title=Scoot Henderson’s Stock Is On The Rise |url=https://hoopseen.com/news/general/201906/scoot-henderson%E2%80%99s-stock-rise |publisher=HoopSeen |access-date=January 20, 2023 |date=June 27, 2019}} On May 21, 2021, he announced that he would [[reclassification (education)|reclassify]] to the 2021 class and join the [[NBA G League Ignite]], declining offers from [[Auburn On November 17, 2021, Henderson made his debut with eight points and six rebounds in a 115–103 win against the [[South Bay Lakers]].{{cite web |title=GLI vs. Lakers - NBA G League Box Score - November 17, 2021 |url=https://www.espn.com/nba-g-league/boxscore/_/gameId/401368489 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 22, 2023 |date=November 17, 2021}} At age 17, he became the youngest player in G League history.{{cite web |last=Davies |first=Spencer |title=NBA G League star Scoot Henderson's aspirations far exceed the hype |url=https://www.basketballnews.com/stories/scoot-henderson-aspirations-far-exceed-any-hype-we-can-give-him |publisher=Basketball News |access-date=January 22, 2023 |date=December 22, 2021}} In his second game, on November 26, Henderson recorded a career-high 31 points, six rebounds and five assists in a 112–110 loss to the [[Santa Cruz Warriors]].{{cite web |title=Scoot Henderson: Explodes for game-high 31 points |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/scoot-henderson-explodes-for-game-high-31-points/ |publisher=[[CBS Sports]] |agency=[[RotoWire]] |access-date=January 22, Weekend]], scoring two points for Team Payton in a 50–48 loss to Team Barry.{{cite web |title=Scoot Henderson: Quiet outing for Team Payton |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/scoot-henderson-quiet-outing-for-team-payton/ |publisher=[[CBS Sports]] |agency=[[RotoWire]]|access-date=January 22, 2023 |date=February 19, 2022}}{{cite web |last=Ganguli |first=Tania |title=Prospects Get a Taste of N.B.A. Life During All-Star Weekend NBA G League season|2021–22 season]], he played 11 games in the G League Showcase Cup and 10 [[exhibition game]]s and averaged 14.3 points, 4.8 rebounds and 4.2 assists per game.{{cite web |last=Irving |first=Kyle |title=G League Ignite prospect Scoot Henderson is much more than a consolation prize to Victor Wembanyama in 2023 NBA Draft 2022}} In October 2022, Henderson represented the Ignite in a [[2022 Metropolitans 92 vs. NBA G League Ignite series|pair of exhibition games]] against [[Victor Wembanyama]], the projected [[List of first overall NBA draft picks|first overall pick]], and [[Metropolitans 92]].{{cite web |last=Woo |first=Jeremy |title=Inside Victor Wembanyama and Scoot Henderson’s Thrilling Showdown in Vegas |url=https://www.si.com/nba/2022/10/05/victor-wembanyama-scoot-henderson-2023-nba-draft-g-league-ignite-metropolitans-92 |website=[[Sports Illustrated]] |access-date=January 23, 2023 |date=October 5, 2022}} In the first game on October 4, he recorded 28 points, nine assists and five rebounds in a 122–115 win.{{cite web |last=Helin |first=Kurt |title=Wembanyama scores 37, Scoot Henderson 28, as both make case to go No.1 |url=https://nba.nbcsports.com/2022/10/05/wembanyama-scores-37-scoot-henderson-28-both-make-case-to-go-no-1/ |publisher=[[NBC Sports]] |access-date=January 23, 2023 |date=October 5, 2022}} On October 6, he left the second game after suffering a bone bruise in his right knee during the first quarter, as his team lost, 112–106.{{cite web |last=Medcalf |first=Myron |title=Ignite's Scoot Henderson has bone bruise, feels 'good and healthy' |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34741249 |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=January 23, 2023 |date=October 6, 2022}} On 3.0: Brandon Miller, Anthony Black are early stock risers |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/2023-nba-mock-draft-3-brandon-miller-anthony-black-are-early-stock-risers-190425634.html |publisher=[[Yahoo! January 10, 2023, he scored 27 points in a 123–122 win over [[Capitanes de Ciudad de México]].{{cite web |title=Ignite Escapes With Win Over Capitanes In Nail-Biting Finish |url=https://ignite.gleague.nba.com/news/ignite-escapes-with-win-over-capitanes-in-nail-biting-finish |publisher=[[NBA G League Ignite]] |access-date=June 20, 2023 |date=January 11, 2023}} In February, Henderson was named [[captain (sports)|captain]] of Team Scoot in the inaugural G League Next Up Game.{{Cite web |date=February 8, 2023 |title=Wolves' Garza And Ignite's Henderson Named Captains For NBA G League Next Up Game |url=https://gleague.nba.com/news/wolves-garza-and-ignites-henderson-named-captains-for-nba-g-league-next-up-game |access-date=March 8, 2023 |publisher=[[NBA G League]]}} He played for Team Jason Terry in the Rising Stars Challenge at [[2023 NBA All-Star Game#Rising Stars Challenge|NBA All-Star Weekend]], scoring four points in a loss to Team Joakim.{{cite web |last1=Taylor |first1=Cody |title=Scoot Henderson ready to jump to the NBA after Rising Stars game |url=https://therookiewire.usatoday.com/2023/02/18/nba-rising-stars-scoot-henderson-draft/ |publisher=Rookie Wire |access-date=June 20, 2023 |date=February 18, 2023}} On March 14, it was announced that Henderson would not play in the final five games of the season. He averaged 17.6 points, 6.4 assists, 5.1 rebounds and 1.2 steals per game in 25 appearances.{{cite web |last1=Givony |first1=Jonathan |title=G League shuts down projected No. 2 NBA pick Scoot Henderson |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/35859223/g-league-shuts-projected-no-2-nba-pick-scoot-henderson |publisher=[[ESPN]] |access-date=June 20, 2023 |date=March 14, 2023}} ==Career statistics== {{NBA player statistics legend}} ===NBA G League=== {{NBA player statistics start}} |- | style="text-align:left;"| [[2021–22 NBA G League season|2021–22]] | style="text-align:left;"| [[NBA G League Ignite|NBA G League]] | 10 || 4 || 31.5 || .460 || .250 || .778 || 4.6 || 4.8 || 1.6 || .3 || 14.7 |- class="sortbottom" | style="text-align:center;" colspan="2"| Career | 10 || 4 || 31.5 || .460 || .250 || .778 || 4.6 || 4.8 || 1.6 || .3 || 14.7 {{S-end}} ==Off the court== On June 15, 2022, Henderson signed a multi-year endorsement deal with [[Puma (brand)|Puma]].{{cite web |title=Welcome to the Fam, Scoot Henderson |url=https://www.puma-catchup.com/young-basketball-talent-scoot-henderson-joins-the-puma-family/ |publisher=[[Puma (brand)|Puma]] |access-date=January 19, 2023 |date=June 15, 2022}} In 2022, Henderson applied for [[trademark]]s on his name and his motto, "Overly Determined to Dominate."
